name: Patch a hole in drywall
blurb: Small holes take filler; anything bigger needs backing. Invisible repairs are 20% filling and 80% feathering and sanding.
gear: Filler or joint compound, and a self-adhesive mesh patch for medium holes
Taping knives — a small one and a wide one
Sandpaper, dust sheet, primer and matching paint
steps: Assess the hole: under 2 cm, fill it; up to 15 cm, use a mesh patch or a plug of new board; larger, cut back to the studs and screw in a new piece.
Cut back any loose paper or crumbling edges to a clean, sound opening.
Apply the backing or patch, then a first thin coat of compound over it, pressing it into the mesh.
Let it dry fully, then apply a second and third coat, each wider than the last, feathering the edges out well beyond the hole.
Sand lightly between coats and finally with fine paper, working with a light held at a low angle to reveal high spots.
Prime the repair before painting, or it will flash a different sheen through the topcoat.
tips: Thin coats, wide edges. One thick blob is what makes repairs visible forever.
Skipping primer is the most common reason a good repair still shows through paint.
Check for pipes and cables before cutting into any wall.
proof: The repaired area is invisible under a raking light after painting.
